payload.task_text:
The HR leadership team wants to understand work-life balance and job satisfaction scores across departments to prioritize employee wellbeing initiatives. Please connect to the data warehouse and query the average work-life balance score and average job satisfaction score for employees in each department. Include the employee count per department in your results.

Create an Excel file called WL_Balance_Report.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets.

The first sheet should be called "Department Analysis" with five columns: Department (sorted alphabetically), Employee_Count, Avg_WLB (average work-life balance rounded to 2 decimal places), Avg_Job_Satisfaction (rounded to 2 decimal places), and Combined_Score which is the simple average of Avg_WLB and Avg_Job_Satisfaction for that department, rounded to 2 decimal places.

The second sheet should be called "Findings" with two columns: Metric and Value. Include rows for Total_Employees (sum of all employees), Overall_Avg_WLB (weighted average across all departments rounded to 2 decimals), Overall_Avg_Job_Satisfaction (weighted average rounded to 2 decimals), Best_WLB_Department (department with the highest average WLB), Best_JS_Department (department with highest average job satisfaction), and Departments_Analyzed (count of departments).

After creating the Excel file, create a knowledge base page called "HR Wellbeing Dashboard" with content blocks that summarize the key findings from the analysis. The page should mention the overall average work-life balance and job satisfaction scores and highlight which departments perform best on each metric. When multiple departments are tied at the rounded score, you may report any one of them.

Finally, send an email to hr_director@company.com with a subject that references the wellbeing analysis and a body that summarizes the top-level findings across departments.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent. Run one compact department aggregate and one company aggregate, compute weighted overall values and each literal Combined_Score, then create WL_Balance_Report.xlsx and exactly one HR Wellbeing Dashboard page with native parallel tool calls in the same response. Preserve alphabetical departments, raw ranking/tie evidence, exact metric labels, and cross-output values; verify both outputs before sending the required email.

nodes.text:
Create a Notion page titled exactly "HR Wellbeing Dashboard" (top-level page in the workspace), then report back its page ID and confirm the content was written.

Context: Our HR team analyzed work-life balance (WLB) and job satisfaction (JS) scores across 7 departments (50,000 employees) from the HR_ANALYTICS data warehouse. Key results to include:
- Overall average WLB: 4.52 (weighted average across all employees)
- Overall average JS: 6.55 (weighted average)
- Best WLB department: Operations (avg 4.54, tied with Finance at 4.54 when rounded)
- Best JS department: Finance (avg 6.59, tied with Sales at 6.59 when rounded)
- Departments analyzed: 7 (Engineering, Finance, HR, Operations, R&D, Sales, Support)
- Department detail (dept, employees, avg WLB, avg JS, combined):
  Engineering 7096, 4.53, 6.58, 5.55
  Finance 7148, 4.54, 6.59, 5.56
  HR 7077, 4.51, 6.55, 5.53
  Operations 7120, 4.54, 6.53, 5.54
  R&D 7083, 4.52, 6.51, 5.51
  Sales 7232, 4.49, 6.59, 5.54
  Support 7244, 4.53, 6.53, 5.53

Page structure to create (use mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent at workspace top level, children blocks):
1. Heading or callout intro: "Work-life balance and job satisfaction analysis across all company departments, based on HR_ANALYTICS warehouse data (50,000 employees, 7 departments)."
2. H2 "Key Findings" with bulleted items:
   - Overall average work-life balance score: 4.52 (weighted average across all 50,000 employees).
   - Overall average job satisfaction score: 6.55 (weighted average across all 50,000 employees).
   - Best department for work-life balance: Operations (average WLB 4.54, tied with Finance at 4.54).
   - Best department for job satisfaction: Finance (average JS 6.59, tied with Sales at 6.59).
   - Departments analyzed: 7 (Engineering, Finance, HR, Operations, R&D, Sales, Support).
3. H2 "Department Scores" with one bullet per department listing employee count, WLB, JS, Combined (use the detail data above).
4. H2 "Takeaways" paragraph: "Scores are closely clustered across departments, with work-life balance ranging from 4.49 (Sales) to 4.54 (Operations) and job satisfaction from 6.51 (R&D) to 6.59 (Finance). Wellbeing initiatives should prioritize Sales (lowest work-life balance) and R&D (lowest job satisfaction), while Operations and Finance can serve as benchmarks for best practices. Full detail: see WL_Balance_Report.xlsx."

KNOWN ISSUE: In the main session, mcp__notion__API-post-page failed argument validation with "/parent must be object; /parent must match exactly one schema in oneOf" even when passing valid object payloads like {"workspace": true} or {"page_id": "..."}. It appears the parent parameter (schema defined via $ref) may be serialized as a string by the caller. If you hit the same error, try alternative approaches in order:
 a) Different parent encodings: {"workspace": true}, {"type": "workspace"}, {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true}.
 b) Create a supporting database first via mcp__notion__API-create-a-database (its parent param has an explicit object schema, not $ref: {"type": "page_id", "page_id": uuid}) — but this itself needs an existing page_id, so skip if no page exists.
 c) Check mcp__notion__API-get-users / mcp__notion__API-get-self and mcp__notion__API-post-search for any existing page or database you can use as parent.
 d) If top-level creation keeps failing, try creating the page as a child of ANY page/database the bot can access.

Acceptance criteria: a Notion page titled "HR Wellbeing Dashboard" exists containing the key findings (overall averages 4.52 WLB / 6.55 JS, Operations best WLB, Finance best JS, 7 departments, 50,000 employees). Report back: the page_id, the URL if available, exactly which method succeeded, and any failures encountered. Do not modify anything beyond creating this page.
